transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-20
Time: 08:00 PT / 11:00 ET
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Damien Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood CSM); Alex Rivera (CTO, Nova Med), Maya Patel (Head of Security, Nova Med), Liam O'Connor (Platform Eng, Nova Med)

Summary:
Quick security posture discovery focused on Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment options. Key topics: SOC2/ISO status, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC and fine-grained access, audit logging & retention, encryption with KMS/HSM, network architecture for Private/VPC, data residency and retention policies. Next steps: share SOC2/ISO artifacts, schedule deep technical session for Private deployment, exchange network diagrams and data retention requirements.

Topics:
- Compliance: SOC2 Type II, ISO27001
- Authentication: SSO / SAML, SCIM, MFA
- Authorization: RBAC / least privilege, token access
- Observability: audit logs, token-level tracing, retention windows
- Encryption: at-rest, in-transit, KMS integration, HSM options
- Deployment model tradeoffs: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem)
- Timelines and POC scope

Transcript:
[00:00] Speaker 1 (Sofia): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Sofia from Redwood. Quick intros?
[00:15] Speaker 2 (Alex): Alex here, CTO at Nova Med. Maya's with me, and Liam. Thanks for setting this up.
[00:22] Speaker 3 (Maya): Hi all. We're mainly here to understand security posture before we talk pricing or pilots.
[00:28] Speaker 1 (Sofia): Totally. We planned to cover SOC2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS, and options for private deployments. Damien will handle the infra/deep tech parts.
[00:40] Speaker 4 (Damien): Hey, quick note — I might say KV cash instead of KV cache sometimes in notes, sorry, my bad.
[00:46] Speaker 2 (Alex): No worries. So starting with compliance, where are you on SOC2 and ISO?
[00:52] Speaker 1 (Sofia): Redwood is SOC2 Type II compliant; we rotate audits annually. We also have ISO 27001 certification. I can send both the SOC2 report redacted and the ISO cert after the call.
[01:05] Speaker 3 (Maya): Great — we'll need the full control matrix for SOC2 and evidence on encryption and key management. Also, do you have a separate report for Dedicated vs Hosted?
[01:16] Speaker 1 (Sofia): The compliance artifacts cover our control plane and hosted infra; for Dedicated and Private we include deployment guidance and customer responsibility matrix. We'll attach a matrix that maps responsibilities for Dedicated/Private.
[01:28] Speaker 2 (Alex): Sounds good. On authentication — we use Okta and SAML for SSO, plus SCIM for user provisioning. How do you integrate?
[01:36] Speaker 4 (Damien): We support SSO via SAML and OIDC, SCIM for user sync, and can enforce MFA via the IdP. For Dedicated, you can bring a dedicated IdP integration inside the VPC.
[01:47] Speaker 3 (Maya): Is RBAC fully configurable? We need role templates and ability to enforce least privilege — also audit trails for role changes.
[01:55] Speaker 4 (Damien): Yes, RBAC is role-based with customizable roles. All admin actions (role grants, key rotations, token issuance) are logged to the audit stream; we can send sample logs.
[02:08] Speaker 3 (Maya): Important that audit logs are tamper-evident and we can push copies to our SIEM.
[02:13] Speaker 4 (Damien): You can forward audit logs to your SIEM via syslog or S3 export; for Private we can set up direct log forwarding into your cloud logging account. We also support immutable write-once logs for certain retention windows.
[02:26] Speaker 2 (Alex): What's the default retention on logs and can we set different windows per dataset?
[02:31] Speaker 4 (Damien): Default is 90 days for standard audit traces, 365 days available as an add-on. You can configure retention per route in Dedicated/Private, and export to long-term storage for compliance.
[02:44] Speaker 3 (Maya): Encryption at rest — do you manage keys or can we bring our own KMS/HSM?
[02:50] Speaker 4 (Damien): Both. Hosted uses Redwood-managed KMS by default, but we support customer-managed keys (CMK) in AWS KMS and also integrations with Azure Key Vault and GCP KMS for Dedicated. For Private we support HSM-based key storage.
[03:04] Speaker 3 (Maya): And are model weights considered customer data? We need clarity on what you persist.
[03:09] Speaker 1 (Sofia): We treat customer prompt/response logs and embeddings as customer data. Model weights are immutable artifacts of the model provider; we don't persist customer-specific model weights. For caching and KV we may store prefixes to accelerate requests — we have controls to not persist sensitive PII by default.
[03:25] Speaker 2 (Alex): What about data residency — can you guarantee EU-only for some workloads?
[03:31] Speaker 4 (Damien): Yes, we have regional hosting and can pin requests to region. For Dedicated/Private we can deploy in a customer-specified region and enforce regional routing.
[03:42] Speaker 3 (Maya): How do you handle deletion requests / data retention policy? We have GDPR and HIPAA constraints.
[03:49] Speaker 1 (Sofia): We support configurable data retention windows; you can request immediate deletion of logs and cached prefixes. For HIPAA workloads we recommend Dedicated or Private so sensitive PHI never leaves your environment. We have a formal DSAs and BAA we can share.
[04:05] Speaker 2 (Alex): Does Redwood run any background model training or using customer data for model improvement?
[04:11] Speaker 1 (Sofia): No. We do not train on customer data. There's a strict policy: customer data is not used for model training. We can include that in the contract and SOC2 scope.
[04:22] Speaker 3 (Maya): If we go Hosted, do you provide per-request trace IDs and token-level cost breakdowns? That's important for our billing reconciliation.
[04:30] Speaker 4 (Damien): Yes, Hosted provides token-level cost breakdown and trace IDs. Dedicated/Private also have the same tracing but you control retention and export.
[04:40] Speaker 2 (Alex): Network architecture for Private — what does the VPC peering look like?
[04:45] Speaker 4 (Damien): For Private we offer two models: 1) Private control plane with customer-managed VPC peering and egress, where inference runs in your VPC (recommended for high compliance), or 2) On-prem package where we ship containers that run behind your firewall. We'll share an example network diagram (link to doc: https://redwood.ai/docs/private-network-diagram).
[05:05] Speaker 3 (Maya): For on-prem, what's the upgrade process? We need predictable maintenance windows and patching schedules.
[05:11] Speaker 4 (Damien): On-prem is orchestrated via our private control plane, we push signed updates; you can schedule maintenance windows and apply updates manually if required. We keep an audit trail of upgrades.
[05:23] Speaker 2 (Alex): Any third-party penetration test results?
[05:27] Speaker 1 (Sofia): We do annual pentests and will share redacted high-level reports and an executive summary.
[05:35] Speaker 3 (Maya): Ok — about RBAC: can we integrate with our existing groups and map to fine-grained roles?
[05:41] Speaker 4 (Damien): Yes — via SCIM we can map IdP groups to Redwood roles; we also support custom role creation and policies by route/model.
[05:52] Speaker 2 (Alex): Latency vs cost — if we pin to Dedicated GPUs in EU, how do fallback policies work if capacity is constrained? We need graceful degradation.
[06:02] Speaker 4 (Damien): We have routing policies — can failover to a compatible model variant in another region or to a lower-cost variant; fallback is configurable per route with SLOs for latency. All failover events are logged to the audit stream.
[06:17] Speaker 3 (Maya): Are there SLA credits for downtime?
[06:20] Speaker 1 (Sofia): Yes, Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; SLA terms are in the Dedicated contract. Hosted has best-effort SLAs on free tiers and formal SLAs for enterprise tiers.
[06:33] Speaker 2 (Alex): Can you summarize the differences in responsibilities between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private?
[06:39] Speaker 1 (Sofia): Sure — Hosted: Redwood manages infra, keys optional CMK; low friction but data resides on our managed infra. Dedicated: reserved compute in our infra, customer gets capacity isolation and more control over retention and keys; we still manage the control plane unless Private enabled. Private: control plane or full on-prem deploy, customer-managed network and keys, maximum isolation. We'll send a responsibility matrix.
[07:00] Speaker 3 (Maya): On logging — do you support immutability? For forensics we need write-once logs for 7 years for some datasets in EU.
[07:08] Speaker 4 (Damien): We can configure WORM-style exports to S3 and object lock for long-term retention. For EU region, we can ensure data residency as well.
[07:19] Speaker 2 (Alex): What about encryption in transit — TLS versions and mutual TLS?
[07:24] Speaker 4 (Damien): We use TLS 1.2+ and recommend TLS 1.3. Mutual TLS is supported for Private and Dedicated endpoints.
[07:33] Speaker 3 (Maya): Do you support IP allowlists and VPC endpoint enforcement?
[07:38] Speaker 4 (Damien): Yes — IP allowlists, VPC endpoints, and private link style connectivity for supported clouds.
[07:46] Speaker 2 (Alex): For token issuance, do you have short-lived tokens and automatic rotation?
[07:51] Speaker 4 (Damien): Tokens are short-lived, you can use ephemeral tokens via our API for session-based interactions. Key rotation is supported and logged; we can rotate CMKs on demand with minimal downtime.
[08:02] Speaker 3 (Maya): If we run POCs with PHI, we'd likely require Dedicated or Private. Do you do BAAs?
[08:09] Speaker 1 (Sofia): Yes, we sign BAAs for HIPAA workloads. We can provision a Dedicated environment scoped to PHI and provide the necessary compliance docs.
[08:19] Speaker 2 (Alex): Any limitations on model types or plugins in Private?
[08:24] Speaker 4 (Damien): Private supports the same model catalog; some closed-source model integrations may have license constraints but we can discuss per-model.
[08:33] Speaker 3 (Maya): How do we get continuous audit evidence? Will you provide log exports and control evidence for our auditors?
[08:40] Speaker 1 (Sofia): Yes, we provide auditor-ready artifacts and can set up direct log exports to your bucket or SIEM.
[08:48] Speaker 2 (Alex): Great. Anything else to discuss?
[08:51] Speaker 3 (Maya): I'd like to see the SOC2 control mapping and the DSAs. Also please include the list of sub-processors.
[08:59] Speaker 1 (Sofia): We'll send the SOC2 report, ISO cert, sub-processor list, and a responsibility matrix. I'll also link the private network diagram and the onboarding checklist.
[09:09] Speaker 2 (Alex): Can we set a technical deep dive next week with Damien to validate network/firewall requirements?
[09:13] Speaker 4 (Damien): Yep — I'll put time on calendar, would like to collect your VPC CIDRs, network ACLs, and any proxy/gateway details ahead of time.
[09:24] Speaker 3 (Maya): We'll also share our data retention matrix and a sample of the data types that could be in prompts.
[09:30] Speaker 1 (Sofia): Perfect. We'll follow up with artifacts and a calendar invite.

Recap / Next steps:
- Sofia: Send SOC2 Type II report, ISO 27001 cert, sub-processor list, responsibility matrix, network diagram, onboarding checklist (due 2027-01-25).
- Damien: Schedule technical deep dive for Private deployment; request VPC info from Nova Med (due 2027-01-27).
- Maya: Share data retention policy and list of regulated datasets (due 2027-01-22).
